title: LogiRx predicts and tests an escitalopram pathway in cardiac hypertrophy
summary: LogiRx, a mechanistic machine-learning model, predicted an off-target serotonin-receptor/PI3Kγ pathway for escitalopram’s antihypertrophic effect. The authors report mechanistic experiments in cultured cardiomyocytes, reduced hypertrophy in a mouse model, and retrospective patient-database associations. The drug and initial compound screen predated LogiRx; patient associations do not establish causation or clinical benefit.
organization: University of Virginia; University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus

evidence.tested: Primary abstract reports experimental pathway validation, cardiomyocyte and mouse outcomes, and patient database associations.
evidence.unknown: Independent replication and broader application are not established by this bounded review.
evidence.ai_role: LogiRx combines a mechanistic network and drug-target data to predict drug-induced pathways for experimental follow-up; the compound screen and drugs were prior inputs.

source_review.scope: Primary PubMed metadata/abstract and publisher full-text PDF indexed result; retrospective human association caveat preserved.
